web_evidence.title: Excerpt from The Last Time They Met by Anita Shreve
web_evidence.note: A sustained, permission-authorized opening excerpt narrates Linda consistently as 'she' while presenting her actions, perceptions, memories, and thoughts; no participating narrator frames the scene.

web_evidence.title: A Love Recaptured in Africa / Anita Shreve reunites high school sweethearts, cleverly merging past and present
web_evidence.note: This contemporary structural review states that the first and last sections use Linda's perspective and the middle section uses Thomas's, while its quoted passages render both characters in third person. It therefore establishes changing focalization, not changing grammatical person, across the novel.

web_evidence.title: The Last Time They Met: A Novel
web_evidence.note: The review identifies an interior passage at the end of the Africa section in which Thomas's thought is rendered as 'he'd,' corroborating third-person narration in the section focalized through Thomas.

web_evidence.title: The Last Time They Met: Reading Group Guide
web_evidence.note: The publisher's guide and author interview verify that the novel proceeds backward through the protagonists at ages fifty-two, twenty-six, and seventeen. It establishes the three-part structure but does not itself explicitly name narrative person.

person_note: The controlling narration is third person with shifting limited focalization: Linda anchors the first and last chronological sections, while Thomas anchors the middle Africa section. The sustained authorized opening, a whole-book structural review with prose examples, an interior quotation, and q00244 agree. The isolated first-person quotations are direct character assertions—potentially speech, thought, letters, or poetry—and do not establish autonomous first-person sections. The main residual uncertainty is their exact local formatting because the quote extraction omits surrounding typography, but credible structural evidence gives no indication of sustained first-person base narration.
